source_docs.title: Distributed training note
source_docs.text: Pipeline parallelism partitions a model across devices by layer. Each device holds a contiguous block of layers and forwards activations downstream. Bubble overhead -- the time devices spend idle waiting for upstream activations -- shrinks as micro-batch count grows.

source_docs.title: Quantization note
source_docs.text: INT4 weight-only quantization preserves activation precision while compressing parameters 4x. The dequantization step adds latency but is hidden by the memory-bandwidth saving.

source_docs.title: CUDA SM note
source_docs.text: The Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) is the fundamental execution unit inside every NVIDIA GPU. The Blackwell B200 contains 128 SMs. Each SM holds CUDA cores, tensor cores, shared memory, register file, and warp schedulers.

source_docs.title: MoE routing note
source_docs.text: Mixture-of-Experts routes each token to k=2 of E=64 experts via a learned gate. Active-parameter count is 2/64 of total, which is what determines per-token FLOPs.

source_docs.title: RoPE note
source_docs.text: Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) encode position by rotating query and key vectors in 2D subspaces. The rotation angle scales with dimension index, giving frequency bands that span short to long range.

source_docs.title: FlashAttention note
source_docs.text: FlashAttention computes attention in tiles that fit in SRAM. The algorithm is exact, not approximate. It avoids materializing the full N x N attention matrix in HBM, which is the dominant memory cost at long context.

source_docs.title: TMA note
source_docs.text: Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) on Hopper handles bulk async copies between global and shared memory. Programmers issue a single descriptor per copy instead of per-thread loads. This frees warps to do compute while the copy is in flight.

source_docs.title: Speculative decoding note
source_docs.text: Speculative decoding pairs a small draft model with a large target model. The draft proposes k tokens; the target verifies in parallel. Accepted tokens are kept; the first rejection forks. Net throughput improves when draft acceptance is high.

source_docs.title: Tensor core throughput note
source_docs.text: Tensor cores execute matrix-multiply-accumulate on small fixed-shape tiles. On Hopper the FP8 tile is m=64 n=8 k=32. Throughput is theoretical peak only when tile shape and dtype line up with the hardware.
